solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Better walk at leisurely pace in much-decreased gravity!

indicators.note: the strolling word sits inside the shrunken gravity word, as the clue says
the gravity word is cut down heavily, keeping only its first two letters

parts.note: taken as written before it is shortened
to amble is to walk slowly and easily

explanation.surface: An astronaut strolls on the Moon, where gravity is much weaker than on Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is a noun here, someone who bets, not the comparative adjective. 'much-decreased' cuts GRAVITY down to GR, and AMBLE goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A better is one who places bets, which is exactly what a gambler does.

clue.text: Regular classes taken by inexperienced driver

parts.note: genera are biological classes, the plural of genus
L is the learner plate shown by an inexperienced driver

explanation.surface: Classes in driving are booked by a learner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' just joins: GENERA is followed by L.
explanation.definitionFit: General and regular both mean usual or normal, as in general practice.

clue.text: Batter often aims for declaration

indicators.note: to batter is to beat out of shape, so the letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: A cricketer regularly targets a declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batter' looks like a cricketer; it is the verb to batter.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a public declaration of aims or policy.

clue.text: Productive hen still held in both hands

indicators.note: the still word is gripped between the two hands

parts.note: L is left, one hand
R is right, the other hand
aye is Scots for always or still

explanation.surface: A productive hen is still held in two hands.
explanation.walkthrough: AYE in the sense 'ever, still' is Scottish and old poetic usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer is a hen kept for laying eggs, the productive part of the flock.

clue.text: Sellers and Lister are in brawl

indicators.note: letters in a brawl are thrown around and mixed up

explanation.surface: Peter Sellers and a man named Lister are fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sellers' reads as the actor's name, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Retailers are sellers of goods to the public.

clue.text: Writer in fictional realm wants start in Republic

indicators.note: the setter's word for themself goes inside the shortened realm
wants here means lacks, so the realm loses its first letter

parts.note: Narnia is the fantasy land of C. S. Lewis's novels
the writer of the clue refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A novelist sets the opening of a story in an imaginary kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is the setter speaking of themself; 'wants' means lacks, not desires.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia is a republic in the South Caucasus, formerly part of the Soviet Union.

clue.text: An old Labour leader in the air

parts.note: Michael Foot led the UK Labour Party from 1980 to 1983

explanation.surface: An old Labour leader is in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is a British political party; Michael Foot was its leader in the early 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Something afoot is in progress or rumoured, in the air.

clue.text: Unusually big cat came in — rubbed round leg

indicators.note: rubbed letters are worn into a new shape, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a round shape looks like the letter O
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A cat comes indoors and rubs against someone's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maine Coon is one of the largest breeds of domestic cat.

clue.text: Elizabethan writer Grey at last promoted

indicators.note: in a down clue the final letter is promoted, moved to the top

parts.note: ashen means pale grey, the colour of ash

explanation.surface: An Elizabethan writer called Grey finally gets promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grey' looks like a surname. The N at the end of ASHEN moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Nashe was an Elizabethan pamphleteer, poet and playwright.

clue.text: Showing anger after welcome is mean

indicators.note: the anger word comes after the welcome word

parts.note: ave is Latin for hail, a greeting
to rage is to show anger

explanation.surface: Getting angry after a greeting is mean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like unkind; it is the mathematical average.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics the mean is the average of a set of values.

clue.text: Mandela party visits New York City

indicators.note: the party calls in on New York, so it is placed inside its abbreviation

parts.note: the ANC, African National Congress, was Nelson Mandela's party

explanation.surface: Delegates of Mandela's party make a trip to New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York City' reads as one place, but 'City' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nancy is a historic city in the Lorraine region of north-eastern France.

clue.text: Some hobbit children disagreed

parts.note: the Tooks are a hobbit family in Tolkien's books, so some hobbits are Tooks
issue means offspring, as in 'died without issue'

explanation.surface: A few of Tolkien's hobbit youngsters had a falling-out.
explanation.definitionFit: To take issue with something is an idiom for objecting or disputing it.

clue.text: Religious campaigner favouring cuts on film

indicators.note: the favouring word cuts into the other pieces, splitting them

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
a film can be a thin mist or haze
being for something means favouring it

explanation.surface: An evangelist who supports budget cuts appears on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' and 'cuts' suggest cinema editing; here a film is a haze and 'cuts' signals an insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A reformist campaigns for change, here in the religious sense of the Reformation.

clue.text: Girl Brisbane lesbians hold back

indicators.note: the held letters are read from right to left
the two words hold the name within them, across the word break

explanation.surface: Women in an Australian city restrain a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' finds ANELE inside brisbANE LEsbians, and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Elena is a woman's given name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Record ushers in unknown Hungarian composer

indicators.note: the record word admits the unknown letter, as an usher admits guests

parts.note: to list something is to record it
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns, so z can stand for one

explanation.surface: A recording introduces an obscure composer from Hungary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' looks like a disc; here it is LIST, and 'ushers in' puts Z inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a nineteenth-century Hungarian pianist and composer.

clue.text: Rhino and bat help to get at provisions

parts.note: rhino and tin are both old British slang for money
an opener is a batsman who opens the innings in cricket

explanation.surface: A rhinoceros and a bat help each other find food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhino' and 'bat' look like animals; in British slang rhino is money, and a cricket opener is a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin opener helps you get at food stored in cans.

clue.text: English work in US appreciated over Ecstasy Complex

parts.note: labour is spelt without the u in American English

indicators.note: in a across clue over means turned back, so the thanks word is reversed

parts.note: ta is British slang for thank you, said when something is appreciated
E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: An English job in America was appreciated more than a drug-fuelled complex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses TA to AT. TA is British informal thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate and complex are synonyms, both describing something intricate with many parts.

clue.text: Alsatians on the loose find mugger

indicators.note: letters on the loose run free and rearrange themselves

explanation.surface: Escaped guard dogs track down a street robber.
explanation.walkthrough: An Alsatian is the British name for a German shepherd dog.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is an attacker, as a mugger is.

clue.text: Greek leader soon accepts brave Frenchman

indicators.note: the soon word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
game means brave or willing
M is the abbreviation of Monsieur

explanation.surface: A Greek leader soon takes in a courageous Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: Brave as an adjective, 'game', is easy to miss when 'Greek leader' suggests a warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon led the Greek forces in the Trojan War.

clue.text: Sportsman revealed spiritual knowledge in forecast

parts.note: a pro is a professional sportsman
gnosis is mystical knowledge of spiritual truths, held to be revealed

explanation.surface: An athlete shows insight into the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealed' looks like a link meaning 'shown'; it is part of the description of GNOSIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A prognosis is a forecast, especially of how a disease will develop.

clue.text: Yokel cut hearts from birds

indicators.note: the hearts letter is cut out of the birds word
the hearts letter is cut out of the birds word

parts.note: pheasant can be plural, a group of the game birds
H is the bridge abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin carves the hearts out of game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: PHEASANT can be plural. H is hearts, as in card games.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a rural worker, often used scornfully of a country bumpkin.

clue.text: Elegantly simple opener from Halifax Town

parts.note: neat can mean simple and elegant, as in a neat solution

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tidy first goal for Halifax Town football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Halifax Town' reads as the football club; 'Town' alone is the definition. Neath is a town in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Neath is a market town in South Wales, near Swansea.

clue.text: Gypsies regularly seen in contemptible place where RC governs

indicators.note: the picked letters appear inside the place word

parts.note: a hole is a squalid, wretched place

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: Travellers are now and then seen in a dump run by the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gypsies regularly' looks like travellers turning up often; it means taking every second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy See is the governing authority of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: As Poe being mysterious for fabulous writer

indicators.note: the letters behave mysteriously, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: Like Edgar Allan Poe, a writer of mysteries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' looks like praise but means writing fables.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author of fables, so he is literally a writer of fables.

clue.text: Disgraceful mark time erased in Greek letter

indicators.note: the time letter is wiped out of the mark word

parts.note: a stigma is a mark of disgrace

explanation.surface: A shameful stain is wiped from a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: New wife probably in jail

parts.note: a bride is a newly married woman
well can mean probably, as in 'it may well rain'

explanation.surface: A newlywed is likely in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridewell was a former London prison whose name came to mean any jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridewell is an old name for a prison or house of correction.

clue.text: New filling for cheese offers solution

indicators.note: the new letter fills the cheese word

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A new sandwich filling with cheese is the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solution' looks like an answer; it is a liquid mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Brine is a solution of salt in water.

clue.text: Another redundant spear-carrier

definitions.meaning: a minor non-speaking actor in a crowd scene

explanation.surface: A further spear-bearer is not needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional or surplus, and as a noun a film walk-on actor.

clue.text: Right man respected in coming into organisation that drives country

indicators.note: the pieces enter the drivers' organisation, splitting its two letters

parts.note: the AA, Automobile Association, is the British motorists' organisation
a gent is a gentleman, a man of respected standing

explanation.surface: A respected right-winger joins a motoring organisation that runs the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, a breakdown and motoring body.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a country in southern South America.

clue.text: North African location where enthusiast returning lives

indicators.note: the enthusiast word comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut
is can mean exists or lives

explanation.surface: A North African spot where a returning fan settles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns NUT into TUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital city of Tunisia, on the North African coast.

clue.text: Hard to exit playhouse — last to leave is antiseptic producer

indicators.note: the hard letter leaves the playhouse word

parts.note: a theatre is a playhouse
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: It is tough to get out of the theatre when you are the last to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to exit' takes H out of THEATRE to leave TEATRE; 'last to' gives E from leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian tea tree yields tea tree oil, used as an antiseptic.

clue.text: New recruit drops from sky through sporting target

indicators.note: the rain falls through the target, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a tee is the mark aimed at in curling and quoits
rain is water falling from the sky in drops

explanation.surface: A novice soldier ducks as things fall from the sky onto a sports target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' looks like a verb; it is the noun, raindrops.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is someone being trained, as a new recruit is.
